fieldMarks: Entirely black, 41–53 cm long, with a strong bill
Voice is the familiar falling caw-caw or caa-caa
behavior: Sociable outside nesting; gathers in communal winter night roosts that can hold thousands of birds
Feeds mostly on the ground; omnivorous, scavenging roads and dumps and taking insects, grain, carrion, eggs and nestlings
Drops hard-shelled mollusks from height onto rocks and coughs up pellets of indigestible food
Resident in many areas; birds breeding north of southern Canada move south for winter
habitat: Semi-open country: farmland, fields, woodland clearings, river groves, shores, towns and city parks; avoids hot desert.
range: Breeds from coastal and southeastern Alaska and across southern and central Canada (north to the southwestern Northwest Territories, northern Prairie Provinces, northern Ontario, south-central Quebec and Newfoundland) south through most of the United States to the Gulf coast and southern Florida.
